node.title: Re: Regex result being defined when it shouldn't be(?)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I haven't fully evaluated or tested your code, but a couple of comments and, if I understood correctly, the answer to your question:

  • For longer regexes, next to /x as you're already doing, I strongly recommend using different delimiters and especially named capture groups ([doc://perlre]) and [doc://%+], as in: my $regex = qr{ (? fo+ ) }msx; "barfooobar" =~ $regex; print "<",$+{foo},">\n"; # prints ""
  • In the regex you showed, if the overall regex matches, then ([@%\$]?) and ([\d]*) will not return undef but the empty string "", because those capture groups will always match at least () (that is, the empty string "").
  • Your expressions like if( defined ($sigil = $1) eq "" ) don't make much sense to me, because you're testing the return value of [doc://defined], a boolean value, against the empty string. If you just want to check for definedness, then write if( defined($sigil = $1) ), and if you want the assignment to $sigil to happen only if $1 is defined, then write if( defined $1 ) { $sigil = $1; ...
  • You might be interested in my module [mod://Config::Perl] ;-)
